head: 663e0cc16d86f5fdf0e019eb27d147708e51538b
source:
Follows the test across formats in #100, whose decision rules were fixed before the data. In doc comments and docstrings, the twelve-rater majority accepted 1 of 28 inline-list findings, against 5 of 16 in Markdown (difference −28 points, −52 to −6), which meets the pre-registered rule for turning a rule off in one format.

The default sits under every user setting: a level for inline-list in `[readcost.rules]`, an override or a flag turns it back on. Markdown, commit messages and the other formats are unchanged. A test covers all four cases.

Uncertain: the cells are small (28 and 16 findings), and the raters are one model family.
feedback:
readcost: 1 sentence in 102 words that may be hard to follow. These are questions, not errors: in a held-out test, model raters said an editor would fix few such findings. Change a sentence only if it reads badly to you, keep its meaning and facts, and leave the rest.
- line 1 [hyphen-compound] coined compound modifier: 'inline-list findings'. Is it hard to follow here? Raters said an editor would fix 0 of 87 such findings, and called 42 more optional. If it is, write the relationship out.
readcost: a finding is wrong? Report it at https://github.com/arclabs561/readcost/issues/new/choose
question: An existing project has a Python docstring and a Markdown page with the same inline list. Which one changes under the new defaults? Can an explicit inline-list setting turn the rule on in the affected format?
key: Only the source docstring changes to ignored by default. The Markdown rule stays active.
Yes. An explicit enabled level, matching override or enabling flag can restore it. One valid route suffices.

head: 44bc26cdbdfde0e4543f70ed21db5c6ddea4c1ce
source:
readcost raised a TypeError in `_markdown` on any inline footnote, `^[text]`. markdown-it's footnote plugin builds the footnote's paragraph at the end of the token stream with no line map. A regex such as `^[a-z]` in a doc comment or a Markdown file parses as one. This dropped three files from the draw for the kinds precision test (#103): a Python docstring, a TypeScript doc comment and a Markdown file.

Fix: before reading, a token without a map gets one. The footnote's paragraph takes the line of its `^[` in the paragraph that holds it; any other token without a map takes the map of the nearest enclosing token that has one. The words after an inline footnote also had wrong offsets, because the reference was skipped by searching for `[^`; that is fixed, and the offsets fuzz test now includes inline footnotes.

Guard: an extraction error on one file becomes a note on that file's result, and any other error on one file is reported for that file. The other files are still checked. The exit status stays 2, as `test_crash_exits_2_not_the_findings_code` requires, so a file that was not checked does not pass.

Tested: the three dropped files (same blobs as the draw records) crash on main and check cleanly on this branch. The regression tests use made-up fixtures with the same shapes, and all of them fail on main. The full suite passes locally.

Not changed: GitHub does not render `^[...]` as a footnote, so in a README a regex like `^[a-z]` loses those characters from its sentence. Turning inline footnotes off (`footnote_plugin(inline=False)`) would change what readcost reads, so it is left for a measured change.
feedback:
readcost: 1 sentence in 277 words that may be hard to follow. These are questions, not errors: in a held-out test, model raters said an editor would fix few such findings. Change a sentence only if it reads badly to you, keep its meaning and facts, and leave the rest.
- line 1 [stacked-nouns] 3 nouns stacked: 'kinds precision test'. Is it hard to follow here? Raters said an editor would fix 0 of 100 such findings, and called 36 more optional. If it is, keep at most two nouns together. Unpack the rest with a preposition or a relative clause, if the result reads naturally; leave an established term as it is.
readcost: a finding is wrong? Report it at https://github.com/arclabs561/readcost/issues/new/choose
question: A batch contains two files. An unexpected internal extraction error occurs in the first. What happens to the second file, and which process exit code should CI receive?
key: The batch still checks the second file.
CI receives exit status 2. A findings-level failure or a successful run is incorrect.
